title: DeLink
tagline: Attestation service based on networking fundamentals to help people succeed in finding a connection for a role, contribution, or relationship in a social graph.
description:
DeLink is an attestation service based on networking fundamentals to help people succeed in finding a connection for a role, contribution, or relationship in a social graph.

DeLink data modeling abstraction is flexible, its relational design uses a bytes32 array to enable a user to connect an infinite number of attestation, which connects the data to numerous other schemas and makes the system versatile.
how_its_made:
DeLink is built on top of Ethereum Attestation Station which as new technology, there isn’t much data on it. This isn’t because it’s a bad technology; rather, it’s because the technology isn’t accessible to everyone.

Currently, technical people can do an attestation, but it’s only feasible for one specific use case - meeting someone in person. While this is an easy-to-understand use case for EAS to generate data and be useful, if you want to go a little further and attest something meaningful, such as that someone has a specific skill, that you are aware of a specific aspect of their identity, or that they are related to or connected to an organization, none of these situations are currently possible.
